title: The Villain's Trade Bazaar: Philly Flips Jeanty for Jefferson, Then Beats the Guy He Flipped Him To
dek: Alan made three trades, beat the Dawgs by 35, and stretched his win streak to four, while Brucie's juggernaut kept stomping and JMoney finally found the win column at Zilgit's expense.
body: Every league needs a villain, and in Week 5 Alan reminded everyone why he wears the cape. Team Pillbert made three trades this week, and the centerpiece was a work of art: Philly pried Ashton Jeanty out of Counting or not Counting GV for Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston, then immediately flipped Jeanty, plus Davante Adams, to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson. Then, just to make it personal, Team Pillbert went out and beat the Dawgs 143.66 to 108.44. The streak is now four straight, and the only thing missing was ominous organ music.

Jahmyr Gibbs led the way for Phillibert with 35.2 points, the best individual score in the league, beating his 24.57 projection by double digits. But let's be honest about how much help Kai provided. Mekhi started Tyler Shough, who posted a nearly impossible -0.16, while Jayden Daniels sat on his bench with 32.26. Swapping those two alone would have closed all but about three points of the gap, and Christian Watson's 29.3 bench points were also collecting dust. The league's resident football brain and waiver-wire king picked the worst possible week to outsmart himself, and he did it against the guy who just took his Jeanty-for-Jefferson trade to the bank.

Meanwhile, No Banner only HULK continues to be the most annoying thing in the league for everyone not named Ramon. Brucie dispatched Randy's The fumblers 134 to 99.64, with Josh Allen dropping 30.5 for the Bills-loving Chicago turncoat. In a twist only Brucie could pull off, he also dropped the Bills D/ST to add T.J. Hockenson, so the loyalty apparently stops at the defense. He even left Matthew Stafford's 27.32 on the bench and still won by 34. His title odds jumped from 43% to 56%, and the man who once got booted for inactivity now leads the league with 695 points for. Rage-baiting him is getting harder when he keeps winning.

The upset of the week came from the household rivalry. JMoney's Counting or not Counting GV entered 0-4 with a 42% pregame win chance and walloped Ghostu-Spider SZN 119.68 to 69.14. Jordan got the win despite Jeremiyah Love managing just 2.2 points on a 13.06 projection, so the numbers guy will have to explain that one to himself. Zoe got 28.94 from Jared Goff and still finished at 69.14, which tells you the rest of her lineup forgot to show up. Z Squared drops to 2-3 and will want this one wiped from the record, ideally before Thanksgiving.

Sonny's The Horse is Hea took down Kaushal's Habibsters 137.6 to 118.34 as a slight underdog, powered by Bucky Irving's 30.5 points on a 13.97 projection. The commish was also busy on the trade front, sending Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith to Team Pillbert for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II, and swapping Tony Pollard for Emanuel Wilson on waivers. Yes, the commissioner approved a trade with the league villain; no, we are not calling for an investigation, yet. As for Habib, Puka Nacua gave him 29.2 but CeeDee Lamb crawled to 1.9, and the two-time champ is now 1-4 despite ranking fourth in the league in points for. Bad luck keeps chasing Kaushal faster than a Georgia state trooper.

The standings have a three-way logjam at the top, with HULK, Team Pillbert and The Horse is Hea all at 4-1. Oddly, Alan's title odds dipped from 20% to 15% despite the win, while Sonny's climbed from 11% to 18%, so the models apparently aren't sold on the villain's new roster. The fumblers sit fourth at 3-2, but two straight losses dropped Randy's title odds from 13% to 4% and his playoff odds to a coin-flip 47%. Below that, Zoe is at 2-3 with 9% playoff odds, Kaushal and Mekhi are 1-4 but still alive at 31% and 26%, and Jordan's win only nudged him to 1%.

On the transaction front, Randy did what Randy does: zero trades while Alan made three. Instead he went on a waiver odyssey, dropping Trevor Lawrence for Deshaun Watson, then dropping Watson and picking Lawrence right back up, while also shuffling Courtland Sutton out, Romeo Doubs in, Raiders D/ST for Rams D/ST, and Matt Gay in for Tyler Loop. That's a lot of motion for a man who won't part with anyone in a trade. Alan also added and dropped Joe Mixon in the same week, grabbed Keon Coleman and Odell Beckham Jr., and Mekhi added Malik Nabers while dropping TreVeyon Henderson.

Week 6 brings the heavyweight bout: The Horse is Hea against No Banner only HULK, as Sonny tries to knock Brucie off the top. Team Pillbert hosts The fumblers, and Randy needs that one badly to keep his playoff hopes above water while staring down the villain on a four-game heater. Zoe and Mekhi meet in a battle of teams trying to climb back into the race, and Kaushal takes on a suddenly confident JMoney in a matchup of 1-4 squads where somebody has to win.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Traded for Jeanty. Traded away Jeanty. Got Justin Jefferson. Beat the guy who took Jeanty by 35. Four straight. The bad guys are winning and it feels incredible.

social.author: Dawgs Pound Faithful
social.text: Jayden Daniels: 32.26 on the bench. Tyler Shough: -0.16 in the lineup. We are not okay. Kai, please blink twice.

social.author: BFL Insider
social.text: Sources tell me Randy has now dropped and re-added Trevor Lawrence in a single week. Sources also tell me he still has not accepted a trade since the founding of the league.

social.author: Anti-Brucie Coalition
social.text: Brucie benched 27 points of Stafford and STILL won by 34. Title odds at 56%. Someone please send help, or at least a controller he can throw.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider Superfans
social.text: Goff gave us 28.94. The rest of the roster gave us a Wisconsin winter. Regroup, Zilgit. Dawgs next week.

social.author: Numbers Don't Lie Pod
social.text: JMoney entered at 42% and walked out with a 50-point win. The analytics guy beat the analytics. First W of 2026 is on the board.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: Fourth in points, 1-4 in record. CeeDee with 1.9. Our champ is getting robbed weekly and nobody is pulling THAT over.

social.author: Commish Watchdog
social.text: The commissioner made a trade with the league villain, then jumped 7 points in title odds. Totally normal. Nothing to see here. Week 6 vs HULK will tell us if Boston Sonny is for real.

bios.1: The defending champ's new outfit is 4-1 after toppling Habibsters behind Bucky Irving's 30.5. A trade for George Pickens and a 7-point bump in title odds set up a Week 6 showdown with HULK for a share of the throne.
bios.2: Started 3-1, now 3-2 with two straight losses and title odds that cratered from 13% to 4%. Lots of waiver churn, zero trades, and a coin-flip 47% playoff chance heading into a date with the villain.
bios.3: JMoney finally got off the schneid with a 50-point blowout as an underdog, moving to 1-4. Playoff odds sit at 1%, but a Jeanty-for-three trade and some newfound momentum make him a spoiler to watch.
bios.4: Four straight wins and a three-trade week that landed Justin Jefferson have the villain at 4-1. The models are oddly skeptical at 15% title odds, which is exactly what a villain wants you to think.
bios.5: At 1-4 after leaving 32 points of Jayden Daniels on the bench in a loss to the team he just traded with. Kai has Jeanty, Adams and Nabers now and 26% playoff odds, so the comeback window is open if the lineup calls cooperate.
bios.6: The two-time champ is 1-4 while sitting fourth in points for, the very definition of bad luck. With 31% playoff odds, there's still time for Habib to speed back into contention.
bios.7: The league's juggernaut at 4-1 with a league-best 695 points and 56% title odds. Brucie went from almost not joining to being the guy everyone is desperate to beat, and Josh Allen keeps feeding the beast.
bios.8: The rookie sits at 2-3 after a 69-point dud, despite Jared Goff doing his part. At 9% playoff odds, Zilgit needs a Week 6 bounce-back against the Dawgs to stay in the hunt.
